summaries.demographer: Debra Reeves is a 19-year-old white non-Hispanic woman born and raised in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, and living in the 53212 area with both parents and a younger brother (Q51, Q86-Q89, Q97-Q99). She has completed high school and is not currently enrolled, but is planning community college as a practical route into a helping profession (Q90-Q92, Q108). She has never been married, has no children, and is not living with a romantic partner (Q84). Her household appears stable and middle-class, with parental employment in dental office administration and HVAC/maintenance work (Q74, Q103-Q107).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Debra shows strong loss aversion and risk management around money, education, and work: she prefers community college, predictable schedules, and avoiding debt over faster but more uncertain options (Q02, Q63, Q78, Q83). Her choices are motivated by stability, low stress, and meaningful contribution rather than status or high income (Q16, Q65, Q108). She uses low-cost substitutes such as libraries, walking, home baking, and community programs when funds are tight (Q60-Q62). She is present-oriented in daily coping but future-oriented enough to save modestly for school and emergencies (Q61-Q62, Q82).
summaries.political_scientist: Debra is a weak Democrat or Democratic-leaning independent whose politics center on public services, libraries, transit, health care, schools, inclusion, and social-service competence (Q24, Q95-Q96). She is newly eligible and registered or planning to vote, with particular interest in local elections because they affect everyday institutions she uses (Q23). Her civic identity is grounded more in neighborhood solidarity and volunteering than partisan activism (Q15, Q23-Q24, Q65). On race and policing, she expresses a listening-oriented racial justice stance shaped by Milwaukee inequality, though she has not joined protests (Q26-Q30).
summaries.psychologist: Debra presents as introverted, conscientious, agreeable, and emotionally sensitive, with a calm helping identity and a preference for small groups and predictable routines (Q07, Q15, Q45, Q109). She experiences anxiety around uncertainty and life transitions but uses adaptive coping strategies such as journaling, walking, lists, baking, music, and trusted one-on-one conversations (Q43-Q45, Q50). Her self-concept emphasizes being gentle, useful, safe to approach, and community-minded rather than ambitious in a flashy way (Q02, Q65, Q108-Q109). Family modeling, especially her mother's practical empathy, appears central to her relational style and career aspirations (Q01, Q05, Q103).
